article.title: Entertainment Weekly Recap
article.summary: ## Entertainment briefing: July 20–25, 2026 - **July 20–25:** Vogue India previewed 19 upcoming OTT releases for July 20–26 across platforms including Netflix, Prime Video and JioHotstar. Titles and projects highlighted included *Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya*, starring Kay Kay Menon; *Musafir Cafe*, starring Vikrant Massey, Vedika Pinto and Mahima Makwana; Kevin Hart comedy *72 Hours*; and *Stuart Fails to Save the Universe*, a *The Big Bang Theory* spin-off. The list also included a third-season WWE backstage documentary, a feature documentary about threatening emails sent to a married California couple, an eight-episode French thriller from the creators of *Ganglands*, and a Brazilian project inspired by the Elize Matsunaga case. - **July 20 onward:** Alt News reported that actors, filmmakers, musicians and other public figures supported youth-led protests in Delhi. Shabana Azmi joined a protest on July 19, met Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, and expressed support for students on hunger strike. The report said she was tear-gassed during the demonstration and posted updates online. Actor and filmmaker Prakash Raj was also reported to have been present. - **During the coverage period:** Pinkvilla reported that Yami Gautam is set to headline *Kahaani 3*, with Sujoy Ghosh returning as director. The film was described as a new story set in the *Kahaani* world and was in pre-production, with shooting timelines not yet locked. - **During the coverage period:** Manoj Muntashir expressed regret over his work on *Adipurush*, calling it the biggest mistake of his life and apologising for the film’s controversial dialogues. He said he felt ashamed of the writing and accepted responsibility for the backlash. - **By July 25:** Reports cited by Google News included *The Odyssey* reaching ₹112 crore in India after eight days and beginning its second week strongly. *Dhamaal 4* was reported to have crossed ₹135 crore after collecting ₹2.25 crore on its third Friday; another report said its India total had later surpassed ₹166 crore. - **July 25:** Google News listings also highlighted reports about Salman Khan sharing gym photographs and a cryptic message, Abhishek Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan being photographed together in New York, and reports that Katrina Kaif could join Prabhas’ *Spirit* after Deepika Padukone’s exit. The *Spirit* casting reports were described as unconfirmed. - **July 24:** WWE coverage reported results from *SmackDown*, including appearances or segments involving CM Punk and Cody Rhodes, a women’s interim-title ladder-match qualifier, and Nikki Bella’s return.

story.title: The OTT Slot

creativeDirection.genre: comedy with a small emotional turn
creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: Two flatmates have one projector slot and opposite movie-night promises, until Vogue India's July 20–26 OTT preview reveals that one beloved choice is not an immediate release at all.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Nikhil wants to lock the projector for his comedy movie night before guests arrive.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: Tara has promised the same slot to a mystery-film crowd and refuses to give up the remote.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: Vogue India previewed 19 OTT releases for July 20–26, while Kahaani 3 was only in pre-production, with shooting timelines not locked.
dramaticSpine.reversal: Tara's preferred Kahaani 3 cannot be tonight's screening because it is not part of that immediate release preview.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: One friend must disappoint their guests and lose control of the shared movie night.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: Tara shifts from defending her choice to admitting she wanted the feeling of a new Kahaani story, not a guaranteed screening.
dramaticSpine.resolution: They choose Musafir Cafe from the preview and share the projector instead of fighting over an unavailable film.

visualBible.setting: A compact Mumbai flat living room on a humid evening, with a ceiling fan, low sofa, tangled charging cables, and a small projector aimed at a blank wall.
visualBible.colorAndLighting: Warm amber practical light from the kitchen mixed with cool blue projector glow; comic shadows stretch across the wall as the argument escalates, then soften at the end.
recurringProps: cushion used as a bargaining token
visualBible.storyArc: The room begins as a playful territory dispute, becomes a frantic negotiation when the release information changes Tara's plan, and ends in warm shared anticipation.
visualBible.referenceImagePrompt: Editorial animated-film still of two Indian flatmates together in a compact Mumbai living room: Nikhil, a lanky man in a mustard T-shirt and checked lounge trousers, clutching a wireless remote; Tara, a woman in a teal kurta and loose black trousers, reaching for it; small projector, steel tea glasses, sofa, charging cables, ceiling fan, blank wall, warm kitchen light and cool blue projector glow, expressive faces, cinematic composition, upper-third caption-safe negative space, no text, logos, or watermark.

cast.role: Flatmate who promised a comedy movie night
cast.voiceProfile: Warm, quick Indian-English male voice with a teasing texture; starts smug and breathless, uses clipped interruptions and tiny victorious laughs, then softens into generous relief by the final line. Give the remote-grabbing moments a playful competitive rhythm.
cast.visualIdentity: Lanky Indian man in his late twenties, mustard T-shirt, checked lounge trousers, messy hair, expressive eyebrows, always leaning toward the projector.

cast.role: Flatmate who promised a mystery-film night
cast.voiceProfile: Low, nimble Indian-English female voice with dry wit and contained disbelief; begins controlled and stubborn, snaps into rapid defensive bursts when challenged, then lands the ending with embarrassed warmth and a resigned smile.
cast.visualIdentity: Indian woman in her late twenties, teal kurta, loose black trousers, tied-back hair, silver hoops, sharp gestures, usually guarding the remote or a steel tea glass.

beats.dramaticAction: Nikhil lunges across the sofa and snatches the remote as Tara reaches for the projector.
beats.turningPoint: The shared movie night becomes a physical tug-of-war before either guest list can be honoured.

visual.caption: Vogue India's July 20–26 OTT preview crashes movie night
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial film frame, Nikhil and Tara tugging opposite ends of one wireless remote over a sofa, small projector wobbling on a stool, Mumbai flat living room, low wide camera, warm kitchen light versus cool projector beam, comic tension, steel tea glasses and cushion visible, clear upper-third caption-safe space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Continuous opening shot in the living room as the remote dispute begins; the projector beam flickers across both faces.
visual.continuityNotes: Establish both characters, wardrobe, remote, projector, sofa, and tea glasses; end with Tara's hand still on the remote.

lines.speaker: nikhil
lines.text: Vogue India's July 20–26 OTT preview has landed—and my projector slot is not negotiable.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Your slot? I promised a mystery night, Nikhil. Release the remote.

beats.dramaticAction: Tara wedges the cushion between them and blocks Nikhil's hand while he tries to plug in the projector.
beats.turningPoint: Their competing promises become a deadline: the first choice connected to the projector wins.

visual.caption: One projector. Two promises.
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial film frame, Tara using a cushion as a playful shield while Nikhil kneels to connect a projector cable, cramped Mumbai living room, medium handheld-style camera angle, blue beam cutting through warm amber light, nervous comic energy, recurring remote and steel tea glasses, upper-third caption-safe space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The camera tracks sideways with Nikhil's cable as Tara physically guards the projector and the argument accelerates.
visual.continuityNotes: Keep the remote between them and preserve the same positions from the opening; advance the action by making the projector connection the contested prize.

lines.speaker: nikhil
lines.text: Pick fast. The preview has 19 releases for this week, and I have guests coming.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Then let me choose Kahaani 3. New story, Sujoy Ghosh back—perfect mystery night.

beats.dramaticAction: Tara grabs her phone to search for the title, then freezes and lowers it as Nikhil pulls the cable free.
beats.turningPoint: The factual update removes Tara's planned film from tonight's options: Kahaani 3 is still in pre-production, with shooting timelines not locked.

visual.caption: Kahaani 3 is in pre-production; shooting timelines are not locked
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial film frame, Tara frozen mid-reach with phone lowered, Nikhil holding the unplugged projector cable, blank wall behind them, close two-shot, cool blue light fading into amber, surprised comic silence, remote and cushion in foreground, upper-third caption-safe space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The continuous shot tightens as Tara discovers the immediate release list cannot rescue her choice; the projector beam dims.
visual.continuityNotes: Carry the cable, phone, remote, and cushion forward; the projector light must visibly weaken to show the plan going wrong.

lines.speaker: nikhil
lines.text: Tara... Kahaani 3 is only in pre-production. Shooting timelines aren't locked.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: So my mystery night is currently a very expensive imaginary night.

beats.dramaticAction: Nikhil reaches for the remote, but Tara catches his wrist, then deliberately places the remote on the cushion between them.
beats.turningPoint: Tara gives up control of the unavailable choice, forcing both flatmates to negotiate from the titles actually previewed.

visual.caption: The remote becomes a peace treaty
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial film frame, Tara placing the wireless remote carefully on the cushion between herself and Nikhil, Nikhil pausing with hand outstretched, compact Mumbai flat, balanced two-shot from sofa height, softened amber and blue lighting, awkward tenderness under comic tension, projector and tea glasses recurring, upper-third caption-safe space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: The same continuous scene pivots from tug-of-war to negotiation as Tara physically creates a neutral zone.
visual.continuityNotes: The dim projector remains on the stool; keep both characters' wardrobe and props unchanged, with the remote now centred on the cushion.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Fine. No ghost movie. Choose from the preview—Musafir Cafe, 72 Hours, anything real.

lines.speaker: nikhil
lines.text: You just surrendered the remote. Are you unwell?

beats.dramaticAction: Tara presses the remote into Nikhil's palm, and he reconnects the projector while she pulls two tea glasses onto the floor.
beats.turningPoint: They turn the failed plan into a shared screening, choosing Musafir Cafe from the preview instead of fighting for an unavailable film.

visual.caption: Tonight's choice: a real release, shared
visual.imagePrompt: Animated editorial film frame, Nikhil reconnecting the small projector while Tara sets two steel tea glasses on the floor and smiles, blank wall glowing softly, wide final camera, warm amber room light with gentle blue projection, relieved intimate mood, mustard and teal wardrobe, remote on cushion, upper-third caption-safe space, no text, logos, or watermark
visual.scenePrompt: Final continuous shot widens as the practical choice replaces the argument and both settle on the floor facing the blank wall.
visual.continuityNotes: Preserve every recurring prop and the softened lighting; end with the projector beam steady and both characters sharing the same side of the room.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Musafir Cafe. Tonight. And next time, warn me before my favourite film is still being made.

lines.speaker: nikhil
lines.text: Deal. But you bring the tea. I lost the remote—and gained a co-host.

interactions.question: Which previewed title would you put first on the projector?
interactions.revealText: The scene chooses Musafir Cafe, one of the titles Vogue India highlighted among the July 20–26 OTT previews; the article does not establish a universal best choice.

story.exit: The projector steadies, the tea is shared, and the unavailable mystery gives way to a real movie-night compromise.
